title: Boiler will not fire: low water cut-off circuit open
equipment: McDonnell & Miller low water cut-offs and water feeders (field-derived draft; probe and float types)

n1.text: Is the burner circuit open, or is the boiler locked out with a low-water light?

r_not.cause: This is not an LWCO problem yet.
fix: Use the general no-heat tree to find why the boiler is not firing.

n2.text: Ask the on-site operator to read the sight glass. Is the water level actually low?

n3.text: Is an automatic water feeder installed?

r_feeder.cause: The feeder is not restoring water.
fix: Have the tech check whether the feeder valve is opening and whether the strainer is clogged.
See the McDonnell & Miller Series 47 and WFE Uni-Match trees for the manual-cited checks.
Also ask why the level dropped (leak, blow-down, relief valve).

r_manual.cause: No feeder, so the level has to be restored by hand.
fix: Make sure the boiler is not overheated before adding water; if the level is below the visible glass, shut down and let it cool first.
Manually feed water to the normal operating level (about halfway up the sight glass). Does the LWCO reset? If it does, find out why the level fell.
If the level is normal but the LWCO still shows low water, restart this tree and answer that the level looks normal.

n4.text: Level is normal but the control still calls low water. Which type of control is it?

n5.text: Ask the operator to press the Test button. Does the LED change or the control reset?

r_cycle.cause: The control is not responding; try a power cycle first.
fix: If it still does not respond, continue with the probe inspection below, then suspect the control itself (internal board failure).

r_probe.cause: The probe is likely fouled with scale, oil or sediment.
fix: Remove power, pull the probe and look for scale, oil or sediment.
Clean it (the field note uses emery cloth or Scotch-Brite), reinstall and retest.
Do not use PTFE tape on the probe threads; make sure the probe does not touch the boiler or pipe wall.
See the Guard Dog RB-122E and FPC-1000 tree for the manual-cited probe checks.

r_float.cause: The float linkage may be sticking or the switch may be failing.
fix: Tap the float chamber gently; sediment can wedge the float linkage.
With power isolated, raise the float by hand and check the switch contacts for continuity (mercury switch or microswitch). Replace the switch head if the contacts stay open.
See the Series 63 tree for the manual-cited float chamber and switch checks.
Never bypass the low water cut-off.
